source_reconstruction_scope: One renderer-independent CharAI::AI_SetTarget(GameObject*,bool) body and its synchronous source call boundaries. It is not integrated into Android or the live Character runtime.
source_semantics: Always stores target at CharAI+0x3c first. If force is nonzero, stores target at +0x40 and returns without debug, owner marker, last-target, dead, or sight work.
For force=false, compares the initial +0x40 target with the argument and clears the owner's 16-bit Character+0x14d0 marker when they differ, before loading/querying DebugSwitches.

Loads and queries exact key IsTracingCharAITarget. The source rereads +0x40 after that query; if the main trace switch is on and the current pointer changed, it queries lowercase isTracingCharAITarget when either old or new pointer is nonnull. The lowercase result is diagnostic and ignored.
The traced old-nonnull to new-null branch writes current target null and returns early. Other ordinary paths store +0x40; null targets return without changing +0x44/+0x48/+0x49/+0x4c.

For nonnull targets, calls Character::GetCharAIId on the then-current owner; the getter clamps invalid IDs to AI row 8 and AI_SetTarget discards the result. It compares freshly read +0x40 with +0x44; a difference clears +0x4c and copies current target to +0x44.
Dispatches current target vtable slot +0x34 as IsDead, stores return XOR 1 in +0x48, reloads +0x40, calls CharAI::AI_IsInSight(GameObject const*) and stores that result in +0x49.
The setter has no Character-only target gate. Character and base GameObject targets use their own vtable +0x34 IsDead implementation; sight/range remains an external source-method boundary.

Any adapter service failure stops at that point without rolling back target/owner/snapshot mutations already completed. The original method is void and these adapter failures are port protocol errors.

service_boundaries.note: Its parameter may be null; the original helper then consults the live CharAI+0x40 target.
